name: Street Perceptions in Greater London (8 Pairwise Indicators)
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (148 Google Street View images re-fetched at random points across Greater London, 2016 or later, 640×480 px, 90° field of view, looking along the road like the paper's views).

Original study: Yang, Krenz, Qiu & Li (2023), ISPRS International Journal of Geo-Information 12(6), 249. 265 participants in London compared pairs of street view images drawn at random from 300 Google Street View images of Greater London. The survey had 8 parts, one per perception (imageability, enclosure, human scale, transparency, complexity, sense of safety, sense of comfort, level of interest), with 5 pairs in each part, and the question wording used here. Choices were turned into 1–5 scores with TrueSkill, predicted city-wide from image segmentation and related to house prices.

Differences from the original study: (1) Images are 148 new Google Street View views, not the paper's 300. (2) In the original survey a pair could be skipped; here each pair needs an answer. (3) Gender and age are asked at the end; the paper reports both but does not show the wording. (4) "the proportion of a human best" in the paper's Human Scale question is written as "the proportion of a human body best".
author: Yang, Krenz, Qiu & Li

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: imageability
elements.title: Part 1 – Imageability: Which street environment do you think is more recognizable and memorable?

elements.name: enclosure
elements.title: Part 2 – Enclosure: Which street environment do you think is more visually enclosed and limits your view?

elements.name: human_scale
elements.title: Part 3 – Human Scale: Which street environment do you think matches the proportion of a human body best and is less intimidating in size?

elements.name: transparency
elements.title: Part 4 – Transparency: Which street environment do you think allows you more to guess what human activity might take place behind the street edge?

elements.name: complexity
elements.title: Part 5 – Complexity: Which street environment do you think is more complex, diverse and visually rich?

elements.name: safety
elements.title: Part 6 – Sense of Safety: Which street environment do you think looks safer?

elements.name: comfort
elements.title: Part 7 – Sense of Comfort: Which street environment do you think makes you more comfortable?

elements.name: interest
elements.title: Part 8 – Level of Interest: Which street environment do you think you are more interested in and would like to visit?
